modelAnswer: Three key steps in developing a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) are: (1) **Identify core features**, determine the essential functionalities that solve the primary user problem, excluding non-critical features. (2) **Build a low-fidelity prototype**, create a simplified model using basic tools or paper-based sketches to test concepts and design options quickly. (3) **Test and gather feedback**, conduct black box testing and user validation to identify functional gaps, usability issues, and requirement misalignments before full-scale development, enabling iterative improvements based on stakeholder input.

stem: Which of the following can be classified as a **low-fidelity prototype**?

keyPoints: Early identification of design and technical flaws
Gathering user feedback and validating requirements
Reducing development risks and costs
Testing feasibility before full-scale development
Improving communication between developers and stakeholders
modelAnswer: Prototyping is important for the following three reasons: (1) **Early Problem Detection**: Prototyping allows developers to identify design flaws, technical issues, and user interface problems early in the development process before significant resources are invested, reducing costly revisions later. (2) **User Feedback and Validation**: A prototype enables stakeholders and end-users to interact with the system and provide feedback, ensuring the final product meets actual user requirements and expectations rather than assumptions. (3) **Risk Reduction and Cost Efficiency**: By testing concepts and functionality through prototypes, developers can validate technical feasibility, reduce development risks, and avoid building features that may not work or be needed, ultimately saving time and development costs.

keyPoints: Printer is an output device that produces hard copies
Laser printer uses a laser beam to form images on a photosensitive drum
Electrostatic image attracts toner particles
Toner is transferred to paper and fused using heat and pressure
Laser printers produce high-quality, sharp prints at high speed
Suitable for high-volume printing with low cost per page
modelAnswer: A printer is an output device that produces hard copies of digital documents and images on paper or other media. A Laser Printer is a high-speed, high-quality printer that uses a laser beam to form images. It works by directing a laser beam onto a rotating drum coated with photosensitive material. The laser creates an electrostatic image on the drum, which attracts toner particles. The toner is then transferred to paper and fused using heat and pressure, producing sharp, clear prints. Laser printers are known for their speed, precision, and cost-effectiveness for high-volume printing.

Tabular layout: enables comparison of data across several records

modelAnswer: Tabular form layout arranges data in rows and columns, displaying multiple records horizontally across the screen with fields as column headers, allowing users to view and compare several records simultaneously. Columnar form layout presents data vertically in a single-column format, displaying one record at a time with field labels on the left and corresponding values on the right, making it suitable for detailed data entry and viewing of individual records.

keyPoints: Difference 1: Black Box tests external functionality without code knowledge; White Box tests internal code logic and structure
Difference 2: Black Box focuses on inputs/outputs and user requirements; White Box focuses on code paths and logical errors
Difference 3: Black Box requires less technical expertise; White Box requires programming knowledge and code understanding
modelAnswer: Black Box testing treats the software as an opaque system and tests functionality without examining internal code structure, focusing on inputs and outputs. White Box testing examines the internal code logic, structure, and paths to verify correct implementation. Black Box testing is performed by testers without programming knowledge, while White Box testing requires detailed code understanding. Black Box testing checks if the system meets user requirements, whereas White Box testing identifies logical errors and code coverage issues. Black Box testing is faster to execute, while White Box testing is more thorough but time-consuming.
